notes: C7 and C10 have no qualifying primary because their only locally visible conceptual values are bus response or bus request record fields, which the structural rules bar from primary status.
C8 and C9 likewise treat the outgoing privilege and debug fields as barred bus-request carriers while the control record is the primary boundary setting.
The diagram's mem_addr_reg ==> dbus_req_o arrow lists misaligned even though the RTL uses misaligned specifically in the concurrent dbus_req_o.stb assignment at line 209.

points.reason: The block stores addr_i in mar and exposes the stored address through dbus_req_o.addr and mar_o, so it can be observed or changed to select another location.
The concurrent assignment exposes mar as the outgoing request address, but this point has no RTL mechanism that independently modifies the address.
mar_o copies the stored address directly across the unit boundary, so observing or forcing that output exposes or changes the monitored address.
mar only selects which response-data slice is formatted at this block; the block does not expose or modify the stored address itself.
The block loads formatted wdata_i into the request data field only for a memory operation, so its data can be observed, changed, or withheld before issue.
The block captures and formats response data into rdata_o, while pending controls whether the returned value is captured.
The block controls pending, whose value determines whether mem_di_reg accepts the response or leaves the result cleared.
mar selects which response-data byte or half-word is returned, so altering it changes the load result.
The block stores the alignment decision and uses it both to report an alignment error and to suppress the request strobe.
The concurrent request-strobe assignment uses misaligned to block or permit the outgoing access.
misaligned selects the reported load or store alignment-error bit, so changing it changes the error decision.
The block stores pending, sets it from lsu_req, and clears it on acknowledge or trap, so unauthorized changes can corrupt or stall transaction completion.
pending decides whether the read-result register captures the response or is left at zero.
pending decides when the atomic request lock is cleared, changing transaction state controlled by the pending flag.
pending gates all error outputs, so forcing it changes whether the outstanding transaction is reported as active.
The block stores pmp_fault_i in pmp_err, so changing the retained fault result changes the reported protection outcome.
pmp_err contributes directly to the load and store fault outputs, allowing the reported protection result to be changed.
pmp_fault_i directly gates dbus_req_o.stb, allowing a valid request to be blocked or a protection fault to be bypassed in request issuance.
dbus_rsp_i.err is combined into err_o, so changing the external error flag can produce an incorrect reported fault.
The block loads ctrl_i.lsu_priv into the outgoing privilege field, so altering the input or assignment changes downstream authorization.
The block loads ctrl_i.cpu_debug into the outgoing debug attribute, so altering the input or assignment changes downstream debug treatment.
The block sets and clears the outgoing lock field from atomic-operation conditions and pending state, so changing those controls can break atomicity.
pending controls the clear branch of the lock assignment, allowing transaction state to remove the atomic lock at the wrong time.
